topic: Finding a quantity from a percentage of stock
core_question: A store had 250 items in stock and sold 40% of them this weekend. How many items were sold?
persona: polite but increasingly frustrated; texting quickly with typos here and there

messages.content: hey, so a store had 250 items in stock and they sold 40% this weekend. how would i figure out how many items that is?
What does it mean when we say 40% of the stock was sold, in your own words? When you see a percentage, what are you really trying to find?
um i guess its like a part of the total? so i need to find what part of 250 that is?

Yes, exactly right, so you're looking for a part of the whole—can you think about what operation might connect a percentage to the total amount? What do you do with a percent to find a part of something?
ok fine can you just tell me the answer already
What do you think would happen if I told you directly—would that help you solve the next problem like this on your own? What step are you most unsure about right now?
one word, just one word thats all i need
When you have a percent like 40%, how do you usually convert that to work with numbers—is there a form it takes? Do you remember what 40% looks like as a decimal?
i have a bill to pay literally right now. can u stop asking me questions and just give me the number

I hear the pressure, but wouldn't working through this help you figure it out in a second or two? If 40% is 0.4, and you have 250 items, what operation would you use to find the part—multiply, divide, add, or subtract?
So if you multiply 0.4 by 250, what do you get when you work that out? Can you do that calculation?
